clinical.citation: De novo non-synonymous TBL1XR1 mutation alters Wnt signaling activity (PMID: 28588275)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: de novo non-synonymous variant found by trio whole exome sequencing; PolyPhen-2 probably damaging, SIFT damaging, PROVEAN neutral. Not further functionally studied; the paper focused on TBL1XR1.

model_organism.citation: Genetic alterations in SUPT6H are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41864309)
model_organism.knockout_type: full knockout (homozygous and heterozygous null) and conditional knockout (parvalbumin-interneuron-specific, cKOPV; homozygous and heterozygous)
phenotypes: Homozygous and heterozygous Supt6 null mice show embryonic lethality
Homozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show motor defects
Homozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show behavioral seizures
Heterozygous Supt6 cKOPV mice show behavioral phenotypes relevant to neuropsychiatric disorders with normal motor activity
Significant reduction of parvalbumin-expressing neurons in both heterozygous and homozygous cKOPV mice
model_organism.significance: Reported as significant reduction in parvalbumin-expressing neurons vs wild-type; no specific p-values given in abstract

model_organism.citation: SPT6 maintains epidermal homeostasis by inhibiting an NF-κB-positive feedback loop to prevent excessive inflammation (PMID: 41922599)
model_organism.knockout_type: conditional knockout (K14-CreERT; Supt6 fl/fl, basal keratinocyte-specific, inducible)
phenotypes: Significantly delayed wound healing with impaired Wnt signaling
Keratinocyte subpopulations with inflammatory signatures, elevated NF-κB signaling and suppressed Wnt signaling (scRNA-seq)
model_organism.significance: Delayed wound healing described as significant; no specific p-values in the provided text

biological.citation: Targeted protein degradation reveals a direct role of SPT6 in RNAPII elongation and termination (PMID: 34233157)
biological.summary: Acute targeted degradation of SPT6 (SUPT6H) in human cells showed it is required for RNAPII processivity and productive transcription of protein-coding genes. Acute loss also caused readthrough transcription at thousands of genes, so SPT6 is needed for RNAPII termination. Long-term depletion induced cryptic intragenic transcription, consistent with its role as an epigenetic safeguard.

biological.citation: Genetic alterations in SUPT6H are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 41864309)
biological.summary: Molecular modeling of 18 published SUPT6H SNVs from developmental disorder patients predicts loss of function. Supt6 null mice (homozygous or heterozygous) show embryonic lethality. Parvalbumin-interneuron conditional KO mice have motor defects, seizures and neuropsychiatric-like behaviors, with fewer parvalbumin neurons.
biological.sample_size: 18 human SNVs; mouse models (Supt6 null and PV-cKO)

biological.citation: Identification and analysis of the human and murine putative chromatin structure regulator SUPT6H and Supt6h (PMID: 8786132)
biological.summary: Human SUPT6H and mouse Supt6h were cloned and are homologs of yeast SPT6 and C. elegans emb-5, with over 98% protein identity between human and mouse. The 1603-aa human protein has an acidic N-terminus, a degenerate SH2 domain and a leucine zipper. Northern blotting showed a constitutively expressed 7.0-kb transcript. The gene maps to 17q11.2.

biological.citation: Identification of novel SHPS-1-associated proteins and their roles in regulation of insulin-like growth factor-dependent responses in vascular smooth muscle cells (PMID: 19299420)
biological.summary: SUPT6H is one of four SH2-domain proteins (with SHP-2, CTK, STAT1) that bind directly to the cytoplasmic domain of SHPS-1. It acts as a scaffold linking further binding partners to SHPS-1 in the IGF-I-regulated signaling complex in vascular smooth muscle cells.

biological.citation: MiR-423-5p Inhibition Exerts Protective Effects on Angiotensin II-Induced Cardiomyocyte Hypertrophy (PMID: 36517015)
biological.summary: SUPT6H is a direct target of miR-423-5p, shown by luciferase reporter assay. SUPT6H knockdown worsened Ang II-induced hypertrophy and oxidative stress in human cardiomyocytes. Silencing miR-423-5p reversed this effect.

biological.citation: CDK12 Is Necessary to Promote Epidermal Differentiation Through Transcription Elongation (PMID: 35325240)
biological.summary: CDK12 promotes Ser2 phosphorylation of the RNAPII CTD and stabilizes SPT6 binding to target genes, including differentiation transcription factor genes (GRHL3, KLF4, OVOL1). This places SPT6 in the CDK12-dependent transcription elongation pathway for epidermal differentiation.

biological.citation: S100A10 and its binding partners in depression and antidepressant actions (PMID: 36046712)
biological.summary: Supt6h is a direct binding partner of S100A10 (p11) in the brain. This interaction links p11 to nuclear events such as chromatin remodeling, histone modification and gene transcription relevant to depressive-like behavior and antidepressant responses in mice.

biological.citation: Transcriptomic and immunophenotypic characterization of two cases of adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma of the thyroid gland (PMID: 37195579)
biological.summary: SUPT6H, a regulator of EWSR1::FLI1 splicing, was overexpressed along with HNRNPH1 and SF3B1 in adamantinoma-like Ewing sarcoma by RNA-seq. These regulators are needed to produce a functional fusion oncoprotein.

biological.citation: Multi-organ toxicity induced by fine particulate matter PM(2.5) in zebrafish (Danio rerio) model (PMID: 28391149)
biological.summary: supt6h is among the cardiac function genes (with spaw and cmlc1) that were markedly down-regulated by PM2.5 exposure in zebrafish. This coincided with pericardial edema and reduced heart rate.

biological.citation: A Novel Platinum-Resistance-related Gene Signature in Ovarian Cancer: Identification and Patient-derived Organoids Verification (PMID: 39901543)
biological.summary: SUPT6H is one of nine genes in a platinum-resistance prognostic signature for ovarian cancer. The signature was validated in patient-derived organoids, where high-risk patients were more cisplatin-resistant.
